live: • ENERGY IS THE BIGGEST HEADLINE DRIVER, AND PUMP PRICES ARE REVERSING. Gasoline is the #1 contributor to 12-month headline CPI (+0.81 pp, just ahead of owners' equivalent rent at +0.77 pp) and PCE (+0.49 pp; +27.9% y/y), but it is falling at a ~31% annualized pace over the last 3 months in both indexes. Upstream energy is still up sharply on a 12-month basis (PPI diesel +78%, jet fuel +67%, finished consumer energy +21%), though those are also falling over 3 months. Airfares are NOT reversing (CPI +22% annualized over 3 months even as jet fuel fell ~31%).

live: • PRICES IN ENERGY-EXPOSED SERVICES ARE RISING, BUT THE BASKET IS NARROW AND IT IS AIRFARES. Transport and delivery services are ~1.6-1.9% of core and add +0.27 pp to core CPI and +0.19 pp to core PCE; airfares (+23% CPI, +19.5% PCE) account for all of it (other transport items net slightly negative). Airfares dominate the energy-exposed transport basket; fuel costs are one possible explanation alongside demand and capacity (the data show rising prices, not causal pass-through). The rest of core runs ~2.1% y/y in CPI and ~2.9% y/y (2.2% annualized over 3 months) in PCE (weighted baskets, not official indexes). Freight PPI (+14%) and trade margins are pipeline risks. This does not explain why core PCE exceeds core CPI.

live: • BEA'S SEPT 30 REVISION SHRANK THE CORE PCE-CPI GAP. Same-month comparison (July): 0.87 pp before the revision, 0.51 pp after; August: core PCE 3.01% vs core CPI 2.45% (0.56 pp). BEA's method changes cut measured portfolio-management inflation from 20.8% to 8.6% and software from 21.2% to 12.3% (July, y/y). Measured as excess over average core inflation, the two now add about +0.25 pp to core PCE (portfolio management ~0.10, software ~0.15; software is 1.2% of core PCE vs 0.04% of CPI): under half of the remaining gap, the rest unexplained here. The gap between core PCE and market-based core narrowed from +0.32 pp to +0.06 pp in July with the revision, and is ~0 in August (3.01 vs 3.03); the two indexes differ in scope and aggregation, so this gap is not the contribution of the excluded items. BEA Table 9.1U (headline only, Dec 2025-Aug 2026): PCE-only items +0.55 pp, shelter weight -0.46 pp.

live: • AI PRICE PRESSURE IS VISIBLE UPSTREAM AND IN COMPUTERS, NOT ACROSS ELECTRONICS, AND THE DATA DON'T PROVE AI CAUSED IT. PPI electronic components +28% y/y and computers +22% (+75% annualized over 3 months); computers are +29% annualized over 3 months in both CPI and PCE (12-month: CPI +8.4%, PCE +8.4%). Against it: phones -14%, semiconductor-industry PPI -3%, hosting PPI +0.3%, application-software PPI -3.7%, and the CPI AI basket is -3.7% y/y. In the PCE AI basket (+10.5% y/y), software is 60% of the starting weight but ~90% of the 12-month contribution; software is +15.6% y/y but only +2.1% annualized over 3 months after BEA's revision.

live: • UNDERLYING TREND IS NEAR 2.2-2.7%, AND MOMENTUM COOLED. Dallas trimmed-mean PCE 2.19% y/y (Aug), Cleveland trimmed-mean CPI 2.6%, Atlanta core sticky CPI 2.7% (2.4% annualized over 3 months). Core PCE annualized over 3 months: July 3.05% before the revision, 2.30% after, 2.05% in August, so part of the cooling is revision and part is new. Breadth (share of core PCE weight rising faster than 3% annualized over 3 months): July ~61% both before and after the revision (61.4% vs 60.3%), then 33% in August, a sharp one-month drop in new data, not a revision effect; core CPI 17%.
